---
title: "On Walking"
date: 2019-03-02 08:15:00 -0700
tags: [essay, habits]
---

I walk most mornings before the house is awake. It isn't exercise, or not only; it's the one hour of the day when nobody needs an answer from me, and I've come to think the answers I give the rest of the day are better for it.

The route doesn't matter much. I go down past the school, along the canal road, and back up the hill by the church, which takes forty minutes if I don't stop and an hour if I do. I usually stop. There's a heron that stands in the shallows below the footbridge, and I've decided it's the same heron every time, though I have no way of knowing.

What I notice, walking, is how little I notice the rest of the time. The light on the water. The man who sweeps the bakery step and never looks up. The way a street sounds different in fog. None of it is important, and all of it is the kind of thing I'd want to have seen.

So I keep walking. Some mornings I think about work, and some mornings I think about nothing at all, and those are the better mornings.
